financialYearNote: 2024-25 (year ended 30 June 2025 for 28 colleges; 31 July 2025 for Emmanuel, Fitzwilliam and Hughes Hall)

definitions.endowmentGbp: Consolidated balance-sheet investments (non-current/fixed-asset investments) at year end, at fair/market value, read from each college's audited annual report and accounts in Recommended Cambridge College Accounts (RCCA) format as filed with the Charity Commission. This is the usual comparable 'endowment' measure; it includes unrestricted funds invested alongside the endowment and investment property, and excludes operational buildings, cash and short-term deposits. It is NOT the same as the balance-sheet 'endowment reserve' (restricted permanent/expendable endowment funds only), which is much smaller for many colleges.
definitions.netAssetsGbp: Total net assets / total reserves (consolidated) at year end, as filed with the Charity Commission (matches the accounts balance sheet in every case checked).
definitions.incomeGbp: Total income for the year from the consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income and Expenditure where the PDF was machine-readable; otherwise income as filed with the Charity Commission annual return (see incomeSource per college). Total income includes donations and new endowments, which can swing a lot year to year.
definitions.students: Undergraduates plus postgraduates (headcount, includes part-time) from the University's postgraduate admissions 'College key facts and figures' page, which states the data come from the University Information Hub 'Student Numbers by College' (2025-26 for 30 colleges, 2024-25 for Girton). The year differs from the financial year, so endowment per student is indicative only.
definitions.endowmentPerStudentGbp: endowmentGbp / students, rounded to the nearest pound.
definitions.noUniversityCompilation: The Cambridge University Reporter no longer publishes a combined 'Accounts of the Colleges' special issue: the 2024-25 and 2025-26 special-issue indexes list only 'Fellows of the Colleges' and the University's 'Financial Management Information'. College accounts were therefore read one by one from the Charity Commission filings.

endowmentDefinition: Investments (non-current / fixed-asset investments) on the consolidated balance sheet at year end, at market/fair value; includes investment property and unrestricted funds invested alongside the endowment

sources.title: Charity Commission for England and Wales, Register of Charities: annual accounts filed by each college (charity numbers per college)
sources.note: Accounts PDFs and register financial-history data were retrieved through the OpenCharities mirror of the register (https://opencharities.uk/ew/<charity number>.json and https://files.opencharities.uk/ew/<charity number>/2025-xx-xx-accounts.pdf), which republishes the documents filed with the Commission.

universityEndowment.name: Cambridge University Endowment Fund (CUEF)
universityEndowment.quote: At 31 July 2025, the net asset value of the CUEF was £4,606.8m (2024: £4,285.9m) of which £4,141.9m (2024: £3,906.7m) is attributable to the University Group.
universityEndowment.sourceRef: Reports and Financial Statements 2024-25, Investments / CUEF section (printed p.27, PDF p.29); balance sheet 'Income and expenditure reserve – endowment' (note 32); net assets and income also on the 2024-25 highlights page
universityEndowment.notes: The CUEF's own financial year ends 30 June; the NAV quoted is as reported at 31 July 2025. About £465m of the CUEF belongs to other investors, including several colleges (e.g. Wolfson), so the University and college figures overlap. The University is a separate body from the colleges; this is for context only.

caveats: College 'endowment' definitions differ between annual reports; this dataset uses balance-sheet investments for comparability, and each college's own headline figure (where stated) is recorded in notes.
Trinity's investments include £1,174.1m of property; St John's figure includes its joint-venture investment.

Several filed PDFs are signed scans; values were read by OCR and cross-checked against a second OCR text and, where available, the narrative financial review. Emmanuel and Hughes Hall were flagged unverified in the first pass; both were re-checked by independent OCR on 2026-11-18 and are now verified. Emmanuel's income is the accounts SOCI total (£27.05m), which is higher than the £22.87m in its Charity Commission annual return because it includes a £4.18m endowment return transfer.
Student numbers are a later academic year (2025-26) than the financial year (2024-25), except Girton (2024-25).

verification.method: For each checked college the filed accounts PDF (sourceUrl) was re-downloaded; investments, prior-year investments and total income were read from the balance sheet / SOCI (pdftotext for text PDFs; fresh tesseract OCR of the cited page for scans: Darwin, Emmanuel, Girton, Hughes Hall, Peterhouse, Trinity, Trinity Hall). Net assets and income were compared with the register financial-history record (opencharities.uk/ew/<number>.json). Student numbers for all 31 colleges were re-read from the postgraduate 'College key facts and figures' page; endowmentPerStudentGbp, endowmentChangePct and the totals sum were recomputed for all 31. On 2026-11-19 every college's 2024-25 investments, net assets and income were also compared with its annual return in the Charity Commission register's bulk extract (registerCrossCheck): net assets agree for all 31, investments for 29 (Clare and Newnham explained in their notes) and income for 30 (Emmanuel explained).
remainingDoubts: Girton (£20,281,000) and Fitzwilliam (£20,281,003) have near-identical total income; both were confirmed from their own SOCI pages, so this is a coincidence, not a copy error.
Emmanuel income: accounts SOCI total (£27.05m) vs Charity Commission return (£22.87m); the choice of definition affects comparisons.

Hughes Hall (£21.0m) and Fitzwilliam (£22.0m) hold large current-asset investments excluded from endowmentGbp, so the balance-sheet measure understates their invested funds relative to colleges that hold such money as non-current investments.
Trinity's investments (£2,704.5m) exceed its net assets (£2,562.5m) because of borrowings; this is correct per the balance sheet, not an error.
Christ's register headline 'latest_income' (£37,334,746) differs from its own 2024-25 financial-year record and the accounts (£39,406,668); the accounts figure is used.

registerCrossCheck.source: Charity Commission register of charities, bulk data extract: annual return Part B (publicextract.charity_annual_return_partb), five financial periods per charity
registerCrossCheck.licence: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
registerCrossCheck.method: Each college's 2024-25 investments, net assets and total income were compared with the same fields of its 2024-25 annual return on the register (assets_long_term_investment, funds_total, income_total_income_and_endowments). 'match' means within £5,000 (the dataset reads some figures in £ thousands); 'explained' means a difference whose cause was read in the filed accounts and is recorded in the college's notes.
